attributes.residual: TWO named clusters, together 12 real lines / 18 fndiff lines, at insns 384/384 with opcode multiset IDENTICAL (classified REGISTER_ONLY by fndiff --clean). CLUSTER A (6 lines): the FindClosestWaypoint result web is colored r26 by our build and r24 by the target, at all three of its uses (`mr. r,r3`, `addi r3,r,0`, `lha r4,106(r)`). The adjacent `camera` web is correctly r25 in both, so this is a single mis-ordered web, not a general pressure difference; the target additionally reuses r24 later in the function for `lbl_80344C6C - 100`, so its allocator packed the two short webs into one register. Declaration-position changes do not move it (axis 3 NEUTRAL). CLUSTER B (6 lines): at the level-up loop preheader the target emits the address materializations in the order gemColors-HA, lfs f31, gPlayers-HA, gemColors-LO, gPlayers-LO; ours emits gPlayers first in both HA and LO. NAMED MECHANISM AND WHY IT IS SOURCE-UNREACHABLE: MWCC ties the EMISSION ORDER of the two loop-invariant address materializations and the CALLEE-SAVED ASSIGNMENT of their two locals to the SAME source ordering, so the two cannot be varied independently from C. Swapping the declarations (axis 1) fixed the emission order exactly -- the relocation sequence became instruction-for-instruction identical to the target -- but simultaneously flipped gemColors/players from r30/r29 to r29/r30, which then cascaded into `add r27,r30,r0` and `add r4,r29,r0` downstream, for a net real 12 -> 18. Splitting declaration from initializer (axis 2) to decouple the two produced the byte-identical outcome, real 18, proving MWCC keys both decisions off the ASSIGNMENT order rather than the declaration order. Every source ordering therefore buys one cluster at the price of the other, at equal magnitude. Remaining escape routes, neither attempted here: a WebFrank REGISTER_ONLY rule covering the r29/r30 swap in the axis-1 variant (which already has the correct emission order and would need only the recolor), or a change in the surrounding webs' pressure that reorders the allocator's choice for cluster A.
